title: Counting lower bound for a conditional sum
statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set, let $p$ be a predicate on $S$, and let $f\colon S \to \bbr$. Suppose $B \in \bbr$ is a lower bound for $f$ on the elements satisfying $p$, that is, $B \le f(x)$ for every $x \in S$ with $p(x)$. Then
\[
  \abs{\{x \in S : p(x)\}} \cdot B \;\le\; \sum_{x \in S} \begin{cases} f(x) & \text{if } p(x),\\ 0 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
hypotheses_covered: p is a predicate on S
f maps S to the reals
B ≤ f(x) for every x ∈ S satisfying p(x)
replaced:
Let $S$ be a finite set, $p$ a decidable predicate, $f : S \to \bbr$ and $B \in \bbr$ with
$B \le f(x)$ for every $x \in S$ satisfying $p$.  Then
\[
  \abs{\{x \in S : p(x)\}} \cdot B \;\le\; \sum_{x \in S} \bigl[\, p(x) \,\bigr] f(x),
\]
where terms failing $p$ contribute $0$.
